sheet-1.description: The first sheet of the Cedarville atlas of July 1912 combines the title cartouche, the water facilities and fire department notes, the index of streets and specials and a small key map of the village (masked out here) with a to-scale map at 50 feet to an inch of the north end of Main Street. The map is drawn as an L: a long strip along Main from Sheppards Avenue at the top-left corner down to North Avenue, and a strip along the north side of North Avenue running off to the right. Because Main is set upright on the page, north points about 55 degrees clockwise of straight up, as the compass rose on the strip shows. The land along Main is residential: frame dwellings of one and two storeys with sheds, wagon sheds, coops, auto houses and stables on deep lots, numbered 501 to 536, with vacant fields beyond on both sides. Along North Avenue, lots 101 to 131, stand the large glass ranges of the Cedarville Green Houses of Mrs. W. H. Henderson, heated by hot water and without lights, and a few dwellings. The village fire department, an engine house for a ladder truck and buckets, stands on North Avenue. Pigeon houses are drawn on the west side of Main near the bottom. The sheet edge carries pointers to sheet 2 for the continuation of Main Street south of North Avenue.
notes: Sheppards Av. is now Willis Lane; Main is Main Street and North Av. is North Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The key map in the top-right corner is drawn at a much smaller scale and is masked out of this part.
Placed from two junctions on Main Street (Willis Lane and North Avenue) only; the North Avenue strip has no junction and its far end depends on the rotation from those two points.

Scale 50 ft. Title, index of streets and specials, and a key map (top right, framed; small scale, masked out) on a to-scale map sheet: Main Street from Sheppards Av (now Willis Lane) to North Av, and North Av to the north-east. North is about 55 degrees clockwise of up. One part (sheet-1).

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 shows Main Street running straight down the left half of the page at 50 feet to an inch, north up, from above East Avenue south to the head of the Mill Pond. East Avenue leaves the east side of Main and runs diagonally up to the right, lined with numbered dwelling lots 9 to 23. Mulford Avenue leaves the west side of Main near the foot of the sheet. The blocks are residential: frame dwellings of one and two storeys, a grocery, a carriage house and many coops, sheds and wagon sheds, with vacant fields beyond the rear lot lines on the west. Main Street house numbers run from 292 to 318 and 101 to 108 on this part. At the bottom the Lannig and Ogden flour mill stands on its head race and tail race beside Mulford Avenue, with notes on its machinery (stand rolls, sifters, grain bins, a purifier), water power, stove heat and no lights; a blacksmith and wheelwright shop, storage of lumber and a pool room stand nearby. Main Street crosses the outlet of the pond on a stone bridge and a trolley bridge, with a stone wall along the pond. A narrow vacant strip down the right edge of this part is marked as fields beyond, next to part 4 of the sheet.
notes: Main is Main Street, East Av. is East Avenue and Mulford Av. is Mulford Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Lannig and Ogden flour mill, water powered, on the head race of the Mill Pond.

sheet-2-3.description: This inset in the top-right corner of sheet 2 shows Main Street at its junction with Sayres Neck Road, north-west of the village centre, at 50 feet to an inch. Main runs up the right edge of the inset and bends away to the south-east below the junction, its east side drawn as a curve; Sayres Neck Road leaves to the left. The inset's own north arrow points up and to the right, and the fit puts north about 31 degrees clockwise of straight up. North of Sayres Neck Road, between it and Main, stands the Central School, a two-storey frame building with a bell tower, heated by stoves and without lights, on block 25, with Main Street numbers 601 to 604. South of the road a single dwelling and a wagon shed stand on the corner lot, with lots 101 to 108 along the road. The sheet's July 1912 Cedarville cartouche is printed in the block north of the road. The rest of the inset is open ground marked no exposure.
notes: Sayres Neck R'd is now Sheppard Davis Road at its junction with Main Street.
Central School, two storeys, bell tower, stoves, no lights.

sheet-2-4.description: The lower right part of sheet 2 shows Main Street north of the village centre at 50 feet to an inch, north up, from Lummistown Road at the top down past Cemetery Road towards the Methodist church. Main runs straight down the part and bends to the north-west at its top, where Lummistown Road leaves to the east. Cemetery Road leaves to the east near the bottom. The blocks are residential, with Main Street numbers 400 to 423: frame dwellings with coops, sheds and wagon sheds, a grocery at the corner by the bend, a cobbler's shop on Lummistown Road and a public garage of tin-clad construction. The First Presbyterian Church, a brick-coloured building heated by hot air and lit by electricity, stands on the east side of Main between Lummistown and Cemetery roads. At the foot of the part, on the west side of Main, is the Cedarville M. E. Church, heated by steam and lit by electricity. Vacant fields lie beyond the lots on both sides.
notes: Lummistown R'd is now Schaffer Avenue at Main Street (Lummistown Road today begins further east); Cemetery R'd is now Prettyman Drive, a service road.

sheet-3-1.description: The left part of sheet 3 shows Main Street south of the village centre at 50 feet to an inch, drawn upright, so that north points about 45 degrees clockwise of straight up. It runs from Railroad Avenue and Commerce Avenue, which meet Main just above the top edge of the sheet, down past New Street to the foot of the sheet. Railroad Avenue crosses the top of the part diagonally. On the east side of Main the former Cedarville Hotel, with a driveway and an ice house, stands in the corner block, followed by a general store, a motion picture house, a cobbler and a blacksmith's shop and a lumber shed. South of New Street the east side has dwellings, wind mills and storage. The west side of Main, lots 233 to 255, is a row of dwellings with a meat market and a five and ten cent store near the top, coops, sheds and wagon houses, and vacant fields beyond. A strip of the next sheet's fire department and smoke house appears in the top-left corner.
notes: Railroad Av. east of Main is now Maple Avenue; Commerce Ave west of Main is now West Maple Avenue; New (arbitrary) is now Stathem Avenue.
The former Cedarville Hotel and a motion picture house.

sheet-3-2.description: The right part of sheet 3 shows Railroad Avenue east of Edgewood Avenue at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned so that the avenue runs up the page: east is up and north points to the left, about 76 degrees anticlockwise of straight up. Edgewood Avenue crosses the foot of the part. The lots on both sides of Railroad Avenue are residential, with house numbers 201 to 241: frame dwellings of one and two storeys with coops, sheds, wind mills and a public garage, and vacant fields beyond on the south side. The north side, between the avenue and the heavy sheet division line, is a single row of dwelling lots backed by vacant fields. At the top a note gives the distance to the Stevens Bros. canning factory drawn in the inset above.
notes: Railroad Av. is now Maple Avenue; Edgewood Av. north of it is Edgewood Avenue and south of it Stathem Avenue.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4 covers the centre of Cedarville at 50 feet to an inch, north up: Main Street running diagonally from the Mill Pond at the top left down to Commerce Street and Railroad Avenue at the bottom, Church Street leaving it to the west, and Edgewood Avenue running east from Main and turning south along the right edge to Railroad Avenue. On the Mill Pond stand the ice houses of A. J. Ogden with an ice run, a sawdust shed, boat houses and a livery. The Osborn Memorial Presbyterian Church and its Sunday school stand on the east side of Main. Lower down Main are dwellings, the post office, drug and dry goods stores, a feed store and restaurant, and the greenhouses of W. B. Jerrell, heated by hot water. Along Edgewood Avenue are dwellings on lots 15 to 42 and a bakery near the corner; the block between Edgewood Avenue and Railroad Avenue holds dwellings, storage buildings and wind mills. The sheet is crossed by heavy lines marking three insets of outlying works.
notes: Church St. is now Church Lane; Commerce St. is now West Maple Avenue and Railroad Av. Maple Avenue; Edgewood Av. is Edgewood Avenue.
Post office on Main Street; W. B. Jerrell greenhouses; A. J. Ogden ice houses; Osborn Memorial Presbyterian Church.

sheet-4-3.description: This inset in the top-right corner of sheet 4 shows the John E. Diament Co. canning factory, located half a mile east of the post office, at 50 feet to an inch. Railroad Avenue runs diagonally up the left side of the inset and crosses the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn as a single track across the inset with two sidings; north of the crossing the avenue continues and a road 32 feet wide branches off to the north-east. The inset's north arrow points up and to the left. The factory lies south of the main track between the sidings: a canning and packing department with can soldering, storage of canned goods, of cans and boxes, of crates and fertilizer, of boxes and baskets and of farm implements, an ice house, a receiving shed, offices of the company and of a commission merchant, a ketchup house and a tin can shop. Notes record five months a year of operation, 150 hands, a night watchman in season and the fire appliances. The freight depot of the railroad stands north of the track, and a public factory school north of the road fork.
notes: Railroad Av. is now Maple Avenue; the Central R.R. of N.J. is the line OpenStreetMap names Southern Main Line.
John E. Diament Co. canning factory; freight depot; factory school (public).

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5 covers the south-west of the village centre at 50 feet to an inch, north up. Main Street runs diagonally from the foot of the Mill Pond at the top down to Commerce at the bottom right, where it meets Railroad Avenue; Franklin runs from the same point at the pond down the left side to Commerce. Between them lie two large blocks divided by Church (arbitrary), which continues west of Franklin as Cedar. In the northern block stand the Oakleaf Academy, lit by kerosene, and the Cedarville Baptist Church with its Sunday school; the southern block holds an undertaker, a livery and carriage house and Bateman Hall, with lodge rooms over a furniture and hardware store and a barber. Commerce crosses the foot of the sheet with a row of dwellings on both sides and open fields beyond; a carriage trimming and painting shop stands at the top by the pond. West of Franklin the lots along Cedar are dwellings.
notes: Church (arbitrary) and Cedar are now Church Lane; Commerce is now West Maple Avenue; Railroad Ave. is now Maple Avenue; Franklin is Franklin Street.

The drawn Franklin and Main meet further south than the modern junction; that junction was left out. The four points used fit with about 5 m RMSE, so the drawing departs from the modern streets by several metres.

sheet-5-2.description: The right part of sheet 5 shows a small district west of Cedar Creek at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned so that north points about 37 degrees anticlockwise of straight up, as the part's own arrow shows. Commerce comes in from the top right and turns into Maple Avenue (Water Street), which runs down the part; a road not named joins Commerce from the north-west at the top, and a road leading to the boat landing leaves Maple Avenue to the west. Cedar Creek and the edge of the Mill Pond are drawn at the top-left corner. The lots are residential: frame dwellings of one and two storeys, carpenter shops, a glass-roofed greenhouse and a wind mill, sheds and storage buildings, with vacant fields beyond on the east. A barn and dwellings stand on the corner of Commerce at the top. The rest of the part is open ground marked no exposure.
notes: Commerce here is now West Maple Avenue, the road not named is Iron Bridge Road and Maple Av. (Water St.) is Jones Island Road.
